title: Mutual Fund Distributors: Your Behavioural Anchor in Investing

faq.q: What is a Mutual Fund Distributor (MFD)?
faq.a: A Mutual Fund Distributor is an individual or entity registered with AMFI (Association of Mutual Funds in India) and authorised by SEBI to facilitate the purchase and sale of mutual fund units for investors. They provide advice on scheme selection and portfolio management.

faq.q: How do MFDs differ from Registered Investment Advisors (RIAs)?
faq.a: MFDs earn commissions from the Asset Management Companies (AMCs) whose funds they distribute, making them product-sellers. RIAs, on the other hand, charge a fee directly from their clients for their advice and cannot earn commissions from AMCs, ensuring their advice is conflict-free.

MFDs typically do not charge a direct fee to the investor. Their remuneration comes in the form of commissions paid by the Asset Management Companies (AMCs) from the expense ratio of the mutual fund schemes.

faq.q: Why is a "behavioural anchor" important in investing?
faq.a: A behavioural anchor, like an MFD, is crucial because human emotions (fear and greed) often lead to irrational investment decisions, such as panic selling during market dips or chasing speculative assets during booms. The anchor helps investors stay disciplined and stick to their long-term financial plan.

faq.q: Can NRIs also benefit from MFDs in India?
faq.a: Yes, Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) can significantly benefit from MFDs in India. MFDs can help NRIs navigate the specific regulatory requirements for NRI investments, understand tax implications, and choose suitable funds aligned with their financial goals back home.

faq.q: How can I verify if an MFD is legitimate?
faq.a: You can verify the legitimacy of a Mutual Fund Distributor by checking their ARN (AMFI Registration Number) on the official website of AMFI (Association of Mutual Funds in India). This ensures they are registered and authorised to distribute mutual funds.
